questions.question: Which Codebeamer feature provides Lean/Kanban support, including Work-in-Progress (WIP) limits?
options: The Agile Planner
The built-in Kanban board
The Release Gantt chart
The Requirements Library
questions.rationale: The built-in Kanban board supports Lean/Kanban practices, including WIP limits. The Agile Planner supports releases, sprints, and backlogs for Agile/Scrum; the Release Gantt chart visualizes schedules; the Requirements Library is unrelated to development methodology support.

questions.question: JAWS wants different teams to use different ways of working within the same Codebeamer project. Which methodology description is correct?
options: SAFe is designed specifically for very large projects with many team members, while LeSS targets smaller teams
Hybrid combines aspects of Waterfall and Agile methodologies
Waterfall allows project phases to overlap and run concurrently
Agile/Scrum requires a single fixed sprint length across the entire organization
questions.rationale: Hybrid combines aspects of Waterfall and Agile. SAFe and LeSS are reversed in the first option (SAFe is typically for smaller teams, LeSS for larger ones); Waterfall is a linear progression where each phase must complete before the next begins, not overlapping phases; Codebeamer does not impose a single fixed sprint length organization-wide.

questions.question: On a task in Codebeamer, what is the purpose of the Planned Effort field?
options: It records the team color used on the Kanban board
It identifies the amount of time required to complete the task and is used to calculate work progress
It defines the workflow transitions available for the task
It sets the WIP limit for the column the task appears in
questions.rationale: Planned Effort identifies the estimated time required to complete a task and is used to calculate work progress and enable logging of spent effort. Team color is a Teams tracker attribute, workflow transitions are configured separately, and WIP limits are configured on Kanban board columns, not on individual tasks.

questions.question: What happens when activity is logged against a task in Codebeamer?
options: The task is automatically reassigned to a new team
The Spent Effort and %Spent/Plan fields are updated based on the logged activity
The task's upstream reference is removed
The release the task belongs to is automatically marked as Released
questions.rationale: Logging activity (date, effort, activity description, and kind) updates the Spent Effort and %Spent/Plan fields, and the history is visible on the Work Log tab. Logging activity does not change team assignment, remove upstream references, or affect the release's status.

questions.question: In Codebeamer's release management, what is true about a sprint?
options: A sprint is a timed unit of development belonging to a release, and shares the same fields and workflow as its parent release
A sprint can only be created before its parent release is saved
A sprint must use a different Release Method than its parent release
A sprint is visible only in the Kanban Board view, not in the Plan or Dashboard views
questions.rationale: A sprint is a timed unit of development belonging to a release and shares the same fields and workflow as its parent release. Sprints are added after a release exists, sprints do not have an independent Release Method, and sprints are visible in the Dashboard and Plan views as well as the Kanban Board view.
